purpose: Lacosamide is used to help control seizures in people with epilepsy. It can be used alone or along with other seizure medications. It is approved for adults and children 4 years and older.
how_it_works: Your brain sends electrical signals to control your body, but in epilepsy those signals can go haywire and cause seizures. Lacosamide works by calming down overactive nerve cells in the brain by slowing a specific channel that controls electrical activity. Think of it like a dimmer switch that turns down the brain's electrical activity so seizures are less likely to happen.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include dizziness, headache, feeling unsteady or clumsy, double or blurred vision, nausea, and tiredness. These are often worse when you first start taking the medication or when your dose is increased, and they usually get better over time.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you feel your heart beating irregularly or have chest pain, as this medicine can affect your heart rhythm. Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can trigger more seizures. It may cause mood changes or thoughts of self-harm — contact your doctor immediately if this happens. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how the medication affects you. Let your doctor know about all other medications you take, as interactions are possible.
typical_dosing: Lacosamide is usually started at a low dose of 50 mg twice a day (morning and night) and gradually increased over several weeks up to a typical dose of 100 to 200 mg twice a day. Your doctor will adjust the dose based on how well it controls your seizures and how well you tolerate it. It can be taken with or without food, and swallowed whole with water.
